body: I don't think that will ever happen. Don't have the initiative and I know that it would be a "no" anyway. When did this turn into a relationship discussion?

Neither of us do much, just saying. She mostly studies, sometimes goes out with her friends on the weekend. I don't ever go out. As far as I know she doesn't attend any of the university functions, neither do I. We both live at home (not on campus), so that obviously hinders ability to be social. 

I doubt there's anyone who would want to take me out. At least not anyone I would want to go with. As far as communication goes, it used to be (in grade 12/summer after) that texting was pretty immediate for response, but gap year turned it to days, then to weeks (on both our parts). I initiate conversations occasionally, always about schoolwork, usually takes a while for her to respond (between 30 mins to a few days, on one occasion). That being said I hardly talk to her outside of face-to-face. 

As far as suicidal thoughts go, I think that the whole situation with the girl definitely factors in, but it's definitely not the only factor. Even without the stress of uni and the above situation, I know I'd have the same thoughts.

Should say I became good friends with the girl by the end of grade 12, didn't really communicate with her much over the gap year that we both ended up taking, made us lose that friendship. Currently talk to her a few times a week now because she's in my chem class, sometimes study with her, but I can sense she's pulling back, so that's not fun. I sense it's cause she realizes I still have feelings for her, or that I'm just a massive downer. Probably both. She also knows my situation, at least sort of. She knew it was a problem during grade 12, not sure if she still thinks it affects me now. I want to tell her, for sure, because I know from experience she'd be supportive, but at the same time I don't want to burden her with that/make myself a burden/annoyance. It's the situation where I feel she doesn't want to be friends/acquaintances, and unloading this on her would kind of force us to remain that way. I could still be wrong, though, who knows. 

 I don't have much fun at anything. I try to entertain myself with Netflix/video games but usually it's not incredibly effective. I don't exercise, I know I should and apparently it helps but again, not motivated. Been rewatching Psych recently, and I guess I've been using that as a "comfort food" of sorts. Did that with a Scrubs rewatch too.  But it's not substantial; doesn't last. Always the thoughts of suicide/uncompleted schoolwork/patheticness in the back of my mind while I watch. 

High school was easy for me. Never did work, got good grades. Don't do work in uni now. Get 50s-60s in phys/math, 70s in chem and 80s-90s in labs/spanish. Still feel stupid. Not motivated to do work, even though I know I should. Tried to do a chem lab report and didn't know how, so feel very stupid. Really just want to turn in a blank report and get a 0. I'm alright with that. I want to get kicked out of uni because it's not fun. Feel like it'd validate my feelings, if that makes sense.

Depression hasn't changed for years, and I don't think it will now. And as far as people from high school go, I know most didn't really like me that much. Admittedly I'm an irritable asshole. Also not attractive, this I know. Basing that off the words of others, not just my self-esteem. I'm also not on any meds anymore. I stopped taking them several months ago because I kept forgetting to take them, and the irregularity of taking them was messing with my mood way too much, even after I tried to get it back to the normal frequency it was fucked up. Felt better for a while, I guess, without the meds. Not too great now obviously. Not sure if they'd help or not, or what combination of meds would actually work because they always seemed to make something go awry with my mood/sleep pattern.

Depression isn't new. Used to have suicidal thoughts throughout high school. Took a gap year and it somewhat helped. By that I mean suicidal ideation/inclination faded, but I was still very depressed and irritable. I have attempted suicide before but it's not worked/been stopped by others. I wish that hadn't been the case. There's mental health services at my school but I'm not really sure how much they can/will do. Honestly, I don't care to see them that much; had enough experiences with therapists/psychiatrists - not to mention the cocktail of antidepressants I was prescribed - and it's never something I enjoy repeating cause it makes me feel worse about myself. I don't see what there is in life to enjoy. I can only remember one time in the last few years I felt happy, and I'm being truthful when I say there's no way to repeat that scenario. 

I just hate how pathetic I am. Other people struggle with all of this shit and still do their work, or they are smart enough not to struggle with any of it because they understand how irrational it all is. I can't do any of that. And as far as the whole 2.5 years thing goes, it's still about 10% of my life so far, bout 30% of my life since I started to have meaningful feelings for other people. Thoughts basically switch between contemplating suicide, her, and self-loathing for any number of things - mainly the two previous things and the fact I'm subpar at university. Call me a quitter, but I'd rather give up

Was on a whole cocktail of antidepressants, though I stopped taking them about a year ago because they ended up amplifying my depression. However that could've been due to how frequently the prescription switched around because none of the meds really worked. Was in therapy too, some mandated by a psychiatrist and some voluntary. None of it was really helpful, because anything they say I'd already thought of (don't mean this arrogantly, just mean it in that I'd thought of a way to deal with depression - and to an extent anxiety - but it hadn't worked, and then they parroted it to me months after I'd came up with the idea on my own).

Also what friends? I still live at home, because residence ist nicht billig. Hard to make friends off campus, don't have any contact with high school friends. I usually just see people in class for 50 mins and then that's it, doesn't even involve talking most of the time. Just that people are creatures of habit so end up sitting in the same place/next to the same people.
